newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:

The United States has refused to participate in a panel appointed by the World Trade Organisation to hear Europe's challenge to U.S. trade sanctions against Cuba, claiming the panel has "no competence" to determine issues of American national security.
The Transportation Safety Board determined that the Boeing 737 is less safe than other airlines because the failure of a single valve controlling the rudder can cause the aircraft to crash.
The New Jersey General Assembly voted to overhaul the state's welfare programME, adding a five-year lifetime limit on cash benefits and incentives to help welfare recipients return to the workforce.

China is planning a deliberately simple funeral for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping in an effort to impart a message of continuity and portray his death as the passing of a retired leader who had already handed over the reins of power.
The people of the China modernised by Deng's economic reforms are busy making money, and few appear moved or fazed by the leader's death.

Senior Western officials said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has presented Russia with a proposal to freeze military forces near Russia's European boundaries in an effort to ease the Kremlin's fears about NATO expansion.

The plight of some illegal Chinese immigrants captured when the Golden Venture smuggler's ship foundered in 1993 has united unlikely allies in York, Pennsylvania, where some of the immigrants are being held at the York County Jail.
Hospital executives and some Congress members are criticising the Federal Government's plan to pay New York State teaching hospitals $400 million to cut the number of doctors they train.
